dialogue.content: こんにちは。ぎりぎりですみません。よろしくお願いします。
dialogue.English: Hello. I apologize for being last-minute. I look forward to our session.

dialogue.content: こちらこそ、ぎりぎりですみません。よろしくお願いいたします。何かこんな事例でやって欲しいとか、ご希望ありますか？
dialogue.English: Likewise, I’m sorry for the last-minute arrangement. I look forward to our session. Do you have any preferences, such as a particular type of case you’d like to work on?

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。今は特にないので、なんでもお願いします。
dialogue.English: Thank you. I don't have anything specific in mind right now, so anything is fine.

dialogue.content: 承知しました。では、よろしくお願いします！
dialogue.English: Understood. Well then, let's begin!

dialogue.content: よろしく願いします！では始めますね。
dialogue.English: Yes, let's begin! I'll start now.

dialogue.content: こんにちは。相談員です。今日はどうされましたか？
dialogue.English: Hello. I'm a counselor. What brings you here today?

dialogue.content: こんにちは。母が甲状腺がんの手術を受けたあと、退院してから元気がなくって。そのことで、ご相談したいです。
dialogue.English: Hello. My mother had surgery for thyroid cancer, and since she was discharged from the hospital, she's been feeling down. I'd like to talk to you about that.

dialogue.content: そうですか。。それは心配ですね。
dialogue.English: I see. That must be worrying.

dialogue.content: はい。医師からは、体調は１年くらいは安定しないかもしれないと言われていますが、浮かない表情をしていることが多く、気になってます。
dialogue.English: Yes. The doctor said her condition might not stabilize for about a year, but she often looks downcast, and it worries me.

dialogue.content: 元気がない姿をみると心配になってしまいますね。。
dialogue.English: Seeing her without her usual energy must be concerning.

dialogue.content: そうなんです。今は自宅療養中ですが、どう勇気づけたらいいのか、、悩んでます。
dialogue.English: Exactly. She’s recuperating at home now, and I’m struggling with how best to encourage her.

dialogue.content: それは、どうやって接すればいいのか、、悩んでしまいますね。お母さまとは一緒に住んでられるんですか？
dialogue.English: I can see how you'd be unsure of how to interact with her. Do you live with your mother?

dialogue.content: はい、実家で一緒に済んでいます。
dialogue.English: Yes, I live with her at my family home.

dialogue.content: 間違えました、住んでいます。
dialogue.English: I misspoke, I meant we live together.

dialogue.content: はい、大丈夫ですよ。一緒にお住まいなら、
dialogue.English: That’s quite all right. If you live together,

dialogue.content: いつも様子を見ることができるとはいえ、心配になりますね。
dialogue.English: even though you can always see how she's doing, it's still worrying, isn't it?

dialogue.content: はい、浮かない表情をしていたらすぐに分かるんです。
dialogue.English: Yes, I can tell right away when she looks down.

dialogue.content: やはり家族だとすぐにわかりますよね。元気がないのは体調不良が原因なのでしょうか。。？
dialogue.English: Of course, as family, you'd notice immediately. Is her lack of energy due to her physical condition?

dialogue.content: 手術後の体調は、そこまで悪くない感じなんです。それより、精神的なもの？のような感じに見えます。
dialogue.English: Her physical condition after the surgery doesn't seem that bad. It seems more like something emotional.

dialogue.content: なるほど、、
dialogue.English: I see...

dialogue.content: 一年は安定しないとのことですが、悪いということではないということですね。
dialogue.English: It was said it might take a year to stabilize, but that doesn't mean it's bad, right?

dialogue.content: 気持の問題だと、、
dialogue.English: So it's more of an emotional issue...

dialogue.content: そうなんです。甲状腺の術後のマッサージなども、ちゃんと自分でやっています。
dialogue.English: That's right. She’s even diligently doing the postoperative thyroid massages herself.

dialogue.content: そうですか、マッサージも自分でされているんですね。
dialogue.English: I see, so she’s even doing the massages herself.

dialogue.content: はい。リンパ節への転移もあり、手術がかなり難航して。６時間は掛かりましたかね。
dialogue.English: Yes. There were also metastases to the lymph nodes, and the surgery was quite difficult. It took about six hours.

dialogue.content: それは、長い手術ですね。。
dialogue.English: That is a long surgery...

dialogue.content: 手術が成功してよかった。
dialogue.English: I’m glad the surgery was successful.

dialogue.content: はい、直後は声が出にくく、あんまり動くこともできずに。それがやや落ち着いてきたこの頃なんですが、何か元気がなくて・・・
dialogue.English: Yes. Right afterward, she had trouble speaking and couldn’t move much. That's settled down a bit recently, but she still seems to lack energy...

dialogue.content: その後も悪くなることもなく、お母さまは自分で回復するためのマッサージもされている。でも、精神的に元気がないとのことですね。声は出るようになり、動けるようにもなったのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: So, her condition hasn't worsened, and your mother is even doing massages for her own recovery. But you're saying she's emotionally down. Has her voice come back, and is she able to move around now?

dialogue.content: そうなんです。身体は動けるようにはなりましたが、声は出しづらそうですね。
dialogue.English: That's right. She can move her body now, but she still seems to have difficulty speaking.

dialogue.content: なるほど、声は出しづらいのか。。
dialogue.English: I see, so speaking is still difficult for her...

dialogue.content: 安心させようと、「絶対大丈夫だから」と何度も言うのですが、イマイチ、伝わっていないような気もします。
dialogue.English: I try to reassure her by saying, "You'll be absolutely fine," over and over, but I get the feeling it's not really getting through to her.

dialogue.content: 元気になって欲しいですものね。それが何か伝わらない感じなのですね。。
dialogue.English: You just want her to feel better, of course. And it feels like that message isn't quite landing.

dialogue.content: はい、声掛けの仕方が良くなかったのかなとか、色々考えちゃって。
dialogue.English: Yes, it makes me wonder if the way I'm talking to her isn't right, and I end up overthinking it.

dialogue.content: どうしてよくないと思われるのでしょうか。。？
dialogue.English: What makes you feel that it might not be the right way to approach her?

dialogue.content: 絶対大丈夫って、何度も言っても、母の表情が晴れる感じがしなかったかんですかね・・・。
dialogue.English: I guess it's because no matter how many times I say 'you'll be absolutely fine,' her expression never seems to brighten up...

dialogue.content: 同じことを何度言っても変わらないとダメなのかなと思ってしまいますよね。。
dialogue.English: When you say the same thing repeatedly and nothing changes, it's easy to start thinking it's not working, isn't it?

dialogue.content: はい。母は昔から、人にあんまり自分の気持ち言わない人なんです。だから表情で見るしかないんですけど、うーん、この言葉あまり響いてなさそうだなと。
dialogue.English: Yes. My mother has always been the type of person who doesn't really tell others how she's feeling. So I have to rely on her expression, and I just get the sense that those words aren't resonating with her.

dialogue.content: なるほど、ではあなたは昔からお母さまの表情を読んでこられたのですね。
dialogue.English: I see, so you’ve long been reading your mother’s expressions.

dialogue.content: そう言われると、そうかもしれませんね。話す相手の眼や表情はじっと見ます。
dialogue.English: Now that you mention it, that might be true. I do tend to watch people's eyes and expressions closely when I talk to them.

dialogue.content: それはとても素敵ですね。相手の方は安心されると思います。
dialogue.English: That's a wonderful quality. I think it must make the other person feel at ease.

dialogue.content: だと良いんですけどね！
dialogue.English: I hope so!

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: 私なら言葉にしなくても表情を見てもらえたらとても嬉しいですよ。
dialogue.English: If it were me, I'd be very happy if someone paid attention to my expressions, even if I didn't put it into words.

dialogue.content: では、お母さまに言葉が響いていないと感じられる場合、今までならどうやってこれらましたか？
dialogue.English: So, in the past, when you felt your words weren't getting through to your mother, what did you usually do?

dialogue.content: ここまで大きな手術は初めてですが、今までだと、気分転換に外食に出かけたりすることが多かったですね。
dialogue.English: This is the first time she's had such a major surgery, but in the past, we often went out to eat for a change of pace.

dialogue.content: 気分転換に外出できたら、気持ちも明るくなれますね！最近は一緒に外出しましたか？
dialogue.English: Going out for a change of pace can really lift the spirits! Have you gone out together recently?

dialogue.content: すみません、外出ではなく外食ですね。
dialogue.English: My apologies, you said eating out, not just going out.

dialogue.content: いやあ、コロナでなかなか外食には行けてないですね・・・
dialogue.English: Well, with COVID, we haven't really been able to go out to eat.

dialogue.content: そうですよね。。なかなかこのご時世ではね。。
dialogue.English: That's true... It's difficult in these times.

dialogue.content: 自宅療養中ということもあって、外には外出できなくて、それで母もストレスがたまってるんでしょうかね。
dialogue.English: And since she's recovering at home, she can't go out, so I wonder if that’s adding to her stress.

dialogue.content: 自宅療養中なのですね。それはストレスがたまると思います。
dialogue.English: She's recovering at home, I see. I imagine that would be stressful.

dialogue.content: 最近、何か気分転換になるようなことはされましたか？
dialogue.English: Have you done anything recently for a change of pace?

dialogue.content: 家でできることで。。
dialogue.English: Something you can do at home...

dialogue.content: そうですよね。ストレス溜まりますよね・・。ただ、まだ退院して1週間なので、家で特に何かすることはないかもしれないです。
dialogue.English: Right, it is stressful... But it's only been a week since she was discharged, so we haven't really done anything special at home yet.

dialogue.content: まだ1週間ですものね。今は生活のリズムを取り戻す時期かもせれませんね。
dialogue.English: It's only been a week, after all. This might be a time for her to get back into the rhythm of daily life.

dialogue.content: そうですよね、母の術後の体調的なところは、気長に付き合っていくしかないのかなぁと思っているところです。
dialogue.English: You're right. I'm thinking that when it comes to her physical recovery after the surgery, we just have to be patient.

dialogue.content: 体調は1年かかるということですし、気長にですね。でも、
dialogue.English: They did say her physical condition could take a year, so patience is key. But,

dialogue.content: 精神的なケアもできればと思ってらっしゃるのですね。
dialogue.English: it sounds like you're also hoping to provide some emotional care for her.

dialogue.content: やっぱり一緒に住んでる家族が元気がないのは、気になります。
dialogue.English: When a family member you live with is down, it's naturally concerning.

dialogue.content: そうだと思います。一緒に楽しく過ごしたいと思いますよね。
dialogue.English: I can imagine. You want to be able to enjoy your time together.

dialogue.content: そうですね、予後は悪くないので、体調は少しずつ回復してくし、気持ちももっと明るく過ごしてもらえたらなと思っています。
dialogue.English: Yes, her prognosis isn't bad, so her physical health should gradually improve, and I just wish she could feel more cheerful as well.

dialogue.content: お家で、お母さまが気分転換できる方法があればいいかもしれませんね。
dialogue.English: It might be good if there were a way for your mother to have a change of pace at home.

dialogue.content: そうですね、気分転換・・・ガーデニングが好きなので、今は窓から庭の花を眺めていますね。それも気分転換になるのでしょうか。
dialogue.English: Yes, a change of pace... She likes gardening, so for now, she's been looking at the flowers in the garden from the window. I wonder if that counts as a change of pace.

dialogue.content: ガーデニング、いいですね！外の空気に触れることもできるし！
dialogue.English: Gardening is wonderful! It's a great way to get some fresh air!

dialogue.content: はい。ただ、今は母が出来ない分、バラの手入れを、私がやらされていますが・・・
dialogue.English: Yes. But since my mother can’t do it right now, I’m being made to take care of the roses...

dialogue.content: そうだったのですね。それは大変。。
dialogue.English: Oh, I see. That must be tough.

dialogue.content: バラの手入れって凄く大変なんですよね。よく母がこの年でやってきたなと思います。
dialogue.English: Taking care of roses is incredibly difficult. I'm amazed my mother has been doing it all these years at her age.

dialogue.content: それはお母さま、すごいですね。それにあなたも
dialogue.English: Your mother is amazing. And so are you.

dialogue.content: 1か月後には、母は体調的にはこれまで通りに過ごせるようになるらしいんです。それまでに、私に何かできることがあればいいんですけど。
dialogue.English: Apparently, in a month, her physical condition should allow her to live as she did before. I just wish there were something I could do for her until then.

dialogue.content: 何かできること。。お庭のバラをお母さまに為に、守ってこられたあなたはとてもお優しいと思いました。
dialogue.English: Something you could do... I think it's very kind of you to have been protecting the garden roses for your mother's sake.

dialogue.content: そうですね、言われてやっただけですが。母のバラを守れたなら良かったです。
dialogue.English: Well, I only did it because she told me to. But I'm glad if I was able to protect her roses.

dialogue.content: 言われたことでも、大変なことを人のために続けるのはすごいことだと思います。
dialogue.English: Even if you were told to do it, continuing to do something difficult for someone else is an amazing thing.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: ガーデニングのお仕事、お母さまと相談して少しずつ一緒にやっていくというのはいかがでしょうか。
dialogue.English: How about discussing the gardening work with your mother and gradually starting to do it together?

dialogue.content: そうですね、1か月を過ぎたら、少しづつ一緒にやってみたいと思います。
dialogue.English: That's a good idea. Once the month is over, I'd like to try doing it together little by little.

dialogue.content: お母さまの気分転換になるといいですね。ここで、少しこれまでのお話をまとめさせていただいてもいいでしょうか？
dialogue.English: I hope that helps lift her spirits. At this point, would it be alright if I summarized our conversation so far?

dialogue.content: はい。
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: あなたのお母さまは、退院されて１週間。体調は悪化していないけど、気分が落ち込んでいる様子で、あなたは心配になっています。1か月後にはこれまで通り過ごせるようになるけど、今はコロナだし外にも出れないし、どうやって元気づけたらいいか、、と思われているのですね。
dialogue.English: Your mother was discharged from the hospital a week ago. While her physical condition isn't worsening, she seems to be feeling down, which is worrying you. She should be able to resume her normal life in a month, but with the pandemic, she can't go out, and you're wondering how you can cheer her up.

dialogue.content: そうなんです。
dialogue.English: That's right.

dialogue.content: そしてあなたは、お母さまを元気づける方法として、今まで気分転換できることをされてきた。
dialogue.English: And in the past, your way of cheering your mother up has been to do things that provide a change of pace.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: きっと、今のお母さまもあなたと気分転換できれば、嬉しいおもいます。
dialogue.English: I'm sure that your mother would be happy if she could have a change of pace with you now, too.

dialogue.content: 安心させようと、「絶対大丈夫だから」と何度も言うのですが、効果はなかったです。
dialogue.English: I tried to reassure her by saying, 'You'll be absolutely fine,' over and over, but it didn't work.

dialogue.content: なるほど、一緒に気分転換。
dialogue.English: I see—a change of pace together.

dialogue.content: はい、コロナだし、声をかけることしかできないと思ってしまいますよね。でも、今までどおりのあなたで、一緒に気分転換できるとお母さまも嬉しいのではないでしょうか。
dialogue.English: Yes, with the pandemic, it's easy to feel like all you can do is offer words of support. But perhaps your mother would be happy if you could find a way to have a change of pace together, just like you always have.

dialogue.content: そうかもしれませんね。外食は無理でも、ちょっといい食事を家で食べることならできるかもしれないです。
dialogue.English: That might be true. We can't go out to eat, but maybe we could have a slightly special meal at home.

dialogue.content: それはいいですね！いつもとちょっと違う演出、家でもできますしね。
dialogue.English: That's a great idea! You can create a special atmosphere at home, something a little different from the usual.

dialogue.content: お寿司とか、母の好きなものでちょっと豪華なものを。いいかもしれないです。
dialogue.English: Like getting some sushi, or something a little fancy that my mother likes. That might be a good idea.

dialogue.content: 好きなものを取り入れるのもとてもいいですね！
dialogue.English: Incorporating her favorite things is an excellent idea!

dialogue.content: 今までの趣味のガーデニングも、身体が動かせなくても、きっと声をかけながら一緒にどうするか考えるだけでも楽しいと思います。
dialogue.English: And with her gardening hobby, even if she can't physically do the work, I'm sure it would be fun just to talk with her about what to do and make decisions together.

dialogue.content: それもいいかもしれないですね。母の指導があったほうが私もやりやすいです。
dialogue.English: That might be a good idea, too. It would be easier for me with my mother's guidance.

dialogue.content: はい、とてもお母さま想いなあなたですし、お母さまもきっと一緒に何かをできれば嬉しいでしょうし、あなたのお優しい思いも伝わるのではないでしょうか。
dialogue.English: Yes, you're so thoughtful of your mother, and I'm sure she would be happy to do something together with you. It would be a great way for your kindness to reach her.

dialogue.content: そうしてみます。ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: I’ll try that. Thank you.

dialogue.content: よかったです。お母さまと良い時間が過ごせるといいですね。
dialogue.English: I'm glad. I hope you and your mother can have some wonderful time together.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: 他になにかお伝えたいことはありますか？
dialogue.English: Is there anything else you'd like to talk about?

dialogue.content: 大丈夫です。相談ありがとうございました。（カウンセラー役、ありがとうございました！）
dialogue.English: No, I'm fine. Thank you for the consultation. (Thank you for playing the counselor role!)

dialogue.content: ありがとうございました。また何かありましたらご相談に来てくださいね。(お時間をいただきありがとうございました！)
dialogue.English: Thank you. Please feel free to come back if anything else comes up. (Thank you for your time!)

dialogue.content: （こちらこそ、ありがとうございました。お疲れさまでした。）
dialogue.English: (Thank you as well. Much appreciated.)

dialogue.content: (これで終了させていただきます。ありがとうございました。お疲れさまでした。)
dialogue.English: (We will end here. Thank you very much. Much appreciated.)
